headline: Garment factory unrest shuts 300 factories; police vehicle set ablaze
summary: Workers demanding higher minimum wages have shut hundreds of factories across Bangladesh, leading to clashes with police and disruptions to major highways and metro services.
details: Around 300 garment factories in Savar, Ashulia, and Gazipur have declared holidays due to widespread labour unrest over minimum wages and other demands, halting production in the industrial belt.
In Savar and Ashulia alone, 177 factories have closed amid the protests. More than 100 factories in Gazipur have also suspended operations, according to police officials.

The protests have spilled onto major roads, with workers blocking the Dhaka-Aricha Highway at Hemayetpur, causing significant traffic disruptions. Violence was also reported in Kaliakair’s Chandra, where a factory warehouse and a law enforcement vehicle were set on fire.

In Mirpur, protests escalated into clashes between workers and police from around 11:30 am to 2 pm. Three metro rail stations—Mirpur 10, Mirpur 11, and Pallabi—were temporarily closed, severely impacting public transport and daily commutes.

headline_marked: Dengue claims [[8 more lives]] in 24 hours as 1,929 hospitalised
headline: Dengue claims 8 more lives in 24 hours as 1,929 hospitalised
summary: Bangladesh records another grim day in its ongoing dengue crisis, with 8 deaths and 1,929 new hospitalizations in the last 24 hours. The total death toll this year now stands at 427.
details: Eight more patients have died from dengue in Bangladesh over the past 24 hours, with an additional 1,929 individuals admitted to hospitals. This brings the total death toll from the mosquito-borne disease to 427 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

October saw the highest monthly toll so far with 174 deaths, followed by September with 148 fatalities. The health directorate reported 831 new hospitalisations in Dhaka Division alone between Saturday morning and Sunday morning.
Admissions were also significant in other divisions: Barishal (213), Chattogram (257), Khulna (259), Mymensingh (92), Rajshahi (185), Rangpur (73), and Sylhet (19).
Nationwide, a total of 136,929 patients have been hospitalised with dengue this year. Of these, 130,388 have recovered and been discharged.

The DGHS has been maintaining records of dengue hospitalisations and fatalities since 2000. The country experienced its worst dengue outbreak in 2023, with 321,179 hospital admissions and 1,705 deaths, surpassing the previous year's toll of over 400 deaths and 102,000 cases.
